Strict optional-property adaptation: approval uses an explicit undefined union; undefined evolution execution, worker auth and missing lesson properties are omitted or deleted. Existing default consumers read equivalent values and JSON serialization is unchanged; own-property reflection is observably different and is not promised equivalent for custom consumers. Adds an inline create() third parameter limited to one own-data recoverySeedText string of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; it is read once before the first await and forwarded only to createWithRecoveryOrigin, while two-argument creation remains the unchanged unmarked store.create path. Also routes marked cancellation to the Store's fresh-generation operation and closes marked continuation in this build: marked resume refuses before cancel clear/save/execution, and marked execute permits only the original queued/revision-0/empty-stages/no-snapshot record, with completed/applied remaining non-executing observations. Initial marked create/execute and unmarked behavior remain on the original paths; no resume tool, work reference or execution wiring is added. Adds a fixed optional own-data recoveryInspector captured once at construction and inspectWithRecoveryLease(): the original Store lease is acquired once, a frozen view exposes only runId/ownerSha256/assertCurrent, the inspector return must be undefined or a native Promise resolving undefined, and the lease is released exactly once in finally with a final intrinsic signal check. The method returns only void and does not unlock execute/resume or authorize continuation.

Strict optional-property adaptation: completed RPC chunk state is deleted instead of assigned undefined. Existing decoder value checks retain their meaning, while own-property reflection can observe absence. Later optional host lifecycle sink: own-data request/port capture, five bounded awaited event categories, throw-on-refusal synchronous guards, intrinsic Promise/AbortSignal checks, one captured cleanup budget, receipt-before-delete and one final-result observation. Optional lifecycle runtime/ownership removals keep the original rm call, observe its raw settlement before any test-only observation delay, join both under the same absolute cleanup deadline and take the actual rm outcome as the removal result; observer failure or an unsettled/expired join latches rejection without later deletion or result observation. The no-sink path retains prior behavior; this does not establish runtime protocol compatibility, stop proof or execution authority.

Upstream store with the existing pure readonly run/events decoders plus a fixed-shape creation-bound recovery codec, an explicit createWithRecoveryOrigin method, an immutable embedded origin and protected-identity save gate, and refusal to roll a marked or origin-declaring primary back from backup. Seeds are capped at 4096 bytes and origins at 8192 bytes before parse or embedded acceptance; initial marked runs are capped at 256 KiB. Adds RunStore.acquireWithContext with an identity-bound frozen lease context and an acquire compatibility wrapper over the original atomic .run.lock algorithm, bounded no-follow owner/primary/cancel reads, a generation-aware marked cancellation request using the original short write lock, and one conditional commitRecoveryInterrupted transition. That transition rechecks the issued lease, raw primary SHA plus file identity, original revision/origin/deadlines, actual AbortSignal, and bounded host currentness at publication and consumption frontiers; it reuses the extracted already-write-locked save body, bounds the serialized next record at 256 KiB, consumes only the exact matched cancel generation, and never executes work. These primitives do not prove user intent, stopped workers, artifact validity, accounting admission or same-build compatibility. The conditional transition binds its lock, reads, backup, primary, cancel and directory sync to the issued lease's captured run directory, so a later runtime store.root mutation cannot retarget it; saveLocked accepts that internal captured directory only for this path, and acquireWithContext captures its root and run directory before its first await. The final intrinsic signal/original-deadline seal runs only after withWriteLock has fully released the short lock, and a post-publication seal failure reports committed state without rollback. Ordinary save behavior is unchanged; marked cancellation writes cancel:<uuid> plus LF (at most 64 bytes) while the original unmarked cancel request remains Controller-owned.
